title: In vitro microfluidic circulatory system for circulating cancer cells
protocol: Culture human colon cancer HCT 116 cells in a T-25 culture flask with DMEM containing 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin under 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Wash the cell suspension with 1X PBS solution to remove dead cells.
Treat the cells with Trypsin for 5 min to detach them from the culture flask.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 1500 rpm for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and re-suspend the cell pellet in fresh DMEM supplied with 10% FBS.

Fabricate a microfluidic silicon master using standard soft lithography technique, designed to contain wide straight channels (100 µm width) and constriction channels (800 µm length, 20 µm width), with a height of 37 µm everywhere.
Prepare the PDMS pre-gel reagent by mixing the polymer base and curing agent at a weight ratio of 10:1.
Vacuum the well-mixed PDMS reagent for 60 minutes to remove air bubbles.
Pour the PDMS pre-gel reagent on the silicon master and incubate it in an oven at 85 °C for 1 hour to gel.
Cut and peel off the PDMS replica from the silicon master.
Punch inlet and outlet holes using a biopsy punch. Clean the surface with tape.
Attach the PDMS replica to a clean glass slide by plasma treatment for 1 minute.
Post-bake the attached microfluidic device at 85 °C for 1 hour.
Insert two segments of polyethylene tubing into the inlet and outlet of the microfluidic device respectively.
Connect the ends of the two polyethylene tubing segments with a large silicon tube using adaptors to form a closed-loop circulatory system.
Wrap the silicon tubing on the rollers of the peristaltic pump.
Pull out one side of the polyethylene tubing.
Sterilize all tubing and microfluidic devices by injecting 70% ethanol for 10 minutes.
Rinse the tubing and device by running 1X PBS to remove air bubbles.
Inject cell suspension into the circulatory system after ensuring thorough dispersion with a pipette.
Re-connect the microfluidic device with the end of polyethylene tubing that has been pulled out for sterilization and injection.
Wrap the silicone tubing on the roller of the peristaltic pump.
Sterilize the peristaltic pump and outer surface of the microfluidic circulatory system by swiping 70% ethanol.
Place the microfluidic device and peristaltic pump into the incubator with 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Start circulation by manipulating the peristaltic pump.
Control the flow rate of circulation by changing the rotating speed (rpm) of the roller in the peristaltic pump.
Use peristaltic speeds of 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 rpm for circulation.
Pull out polyethylene tubing when circulation is done.
Insert a syringe needle into one side of the tubing and place the other side into a petri dish or centrifuge tube.
Use a syringe containing sterile air to blow the cell suspension out.
Treat the collected cells with Live/Dead assays after 1 hour sedimentation.
Determine cell viability by using confocal microscope.
Collect cell suspension in a petri dish containing fresh DMEM culture medium for determining cell proliferation.
Incubate the sample for 2 hours in an on-stage incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Record time-lapse video of cell growth in a petri dish for 16 hours using a camera mounted on a fluorescent microscope.
Collect cell suspension from circulation into a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes. Remove the supernatant.
Disperse the cell pellet into TRIZOL reagent.
Incubate the homogenized samples for 5 minutes at 15 to 30°C.
Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIZOL reagent.
Cap sample tubes securely.
Shake tubes vigorously by hand for 15 seconds and incubate them at 15 to 30°C for 2 to 3 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples at no more than 12,000 x g for 15 minutes at 2 to 8°C.
Transfer 350 μL of aqueous phase to a fresh tube.
Precipitate the RNA from the aqueous phase by mixing with isopropyl alcohol.
Use 0.5 mL of isopropyl alcohol per 1 mL of TRIZOL reagent used for the initial homogenization.
Incubate samples at 15 to 30°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at no more than 12,000 x g for 10 minutes at 2 to 8°C.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Wash the RNA pellet once with 75% ethanol, adding at least 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIZOL reagent used for the initial homogenization.
Mix the sample by vortexing.
Centrifuge at no more than 7,500 x g for 5 minutes at 2 to 8°C.
Briefly dry the pellet (air-dry for 5-10 minutes).
Dissolve RNA in 40-50 μL RNase-free water or 0.5% SDS solution by passing the solution a few times through a pipette tip.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 55 to 60°C.
RNA can also be redissolved in 100% deionized formamide and stored at -70°C.
Use RNase-free water as blank and baseline for Nanodot machine to obtain concentration of RNA in samples, placing 1 μL sample on sensor after cleaning.
Use protocol from MAXIMA first strand cDNA synthesis kit for RT-qPCR.

Calculate the amount of template RNA required using the following calculation: X = concentration obtained from Nanodot; Y = amount of template solution needed; Amount of template required = 5 μg/(X/1000) = Y μL.
Follow MAXIMA protocol and add reagents to a sterile, RNAse-free tube on ice in the order described.
Mix gently and centrifuge.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 25°C followed by 15 minutes at 50°C.
Terminate reaction by heating at 85°C for 5 minutes using program already set on PCR machine.
Calculate the amount of substrates required for RT-PCR assay.
Run RT-PCR assay on RT-PCR machine.
Open data file in analysis software.
Click on quantitation option.
Select samples from quantitation drop-down menu.
Copy selected sample data to clipboard.
Open excel file.
Paste copied data into excel file.
Sort data by sample name.
Calculate average of each sample set.
Calculate standard deviation of each sample set.
Normalize each average to actin average.
Create data table in spreadsheet.
Populate data table with normalized values.
Normalize each data set to control value.
Obtain final data using formula: power(2, - (normalized data)).
Plot the final data.
